context: The Active Prompt page currently has a session storage mechanism that remembers the user's last selected execution-mode radio button. However, the requirement states that radio buttons should 'always reflect the value of execution-mode entry in work-iteration-registry.json'. This creates questions about how the two mechanisms should interact.

questions.question-text: Should the session storage mechanism for execution-mode be removed completely, or should it be kept but subordinated to the registry value?

options.label: Remove session storage entirely - always show registry value
options.pros: Simplest solution, ensures strict compliance with requirement, eliminates any possibility of confusion between saved state and registry state, makes behavior predictable and deterministic
options.cons: User loses convenience of having their last selection remembered across page refreshes when working on a prompt, may need to re-select mode more frequently

options.label: Keep session storage but always override with registry value on refresh
options.pros: Maintains existing infrastructure, allows for potential future enhancements where session storage might be useful
options.cons: More complex code, session storage becomes unused/redundant, adds maintenance burden without clear benefit

options.label: Keep session storage for user convenience but clear it when registry changes
options.pros: Provides best user experience by remembering selections during active work while respecting registry changes, balances convenience with correctness
options.cons: Most complex solution, requires detecting registry changes, may have edge cases where sync fails

questions.recommendation-rationale: The requirement explicitly states radio buttons should 'always' reflect the registry value. The word 'always' suggests strict compliance without exceptions. Additionally, execution-mode changes are typically triggered by script execution or deliberate user action through the UI, not frequent enough to warrant session persistence. Removing the session storage eliminates complexity and ensures the UI always shows the authoritative state from the registry.

questions.question-text: The refreshActivePromptStatuses() function currently runs every 2 seconds to update status indicators. Should it also update the execution-mode radio buttons on each refresh?

options.label: Yes - update radio buttons on every 2-second refresh
options.pros: Ensures radio buttons are always in sync with registry even if changed externally, provides real-time updates, aligns with requirement for 'always' reflecting registry value
options.cons: Could be jarring if user is about to click a radio button and it changes, uses more CPU cycles for potentially unnecessary updates

options.label: No - only update radio buttons when page loads or after mode change
options.pros: More stable UI, no interruption to user actions, sufficient for normal workflow where mode changes are user-initiated
options.cons: Radio buttons won't reflect external changes until page reload, doesn't fully satisfy 'always' requirement if registry is modified by external process

options.label: Hybrid - update on refresh but only if registry value changed
options.pros: Best of both worlds - updates when needed but avoids unnecessary DOM manipulation, responsive to changes while being efficient
options.cons: Requires tracking previous value to detect changes, adds slight complexity

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt mentions 'Every refresh of the statuses of the files in Active Prompt should include radio buttons update as well', which indicates updates should happen during the refresh cycle. However, updating only when the value actually changes is more efficient and avoids unnecessary DOM manipulation. This approach balances the requirement with good UX practices.

questions.question-text: When the updateExecutionMode() function is called (user clicks a radio button), should it continue to save the mode to session storage, or should this be removed?

options.label: Remove session storage save entirely
options.pros: Consistent with removing session storage dependency, simpler code, reduces potential for state desynchronization
options.cons: None if we're removing session storage mechanism

options.label: Keep session storage save for now but don't use it
options.pros: Minimal code changes, allows easy rollback if needed
options.cons: Writes unused data, confusing for future maintainers, technical debt

questions.recommendation-rationale: If we decide to remove session storage usage for execution-mode (as suggested in Q1), then we should also remove the code that saves to session storage. This maintains code cleanliness and eliminates dead code. There's no benefit to storing data that won't be used.
